title: TSA Braces for 17.6 Million Flyers. Giuliani Gets a Medal. Anthropic Slips.
subject: TSA Braces for 17.6 Million Flyers. Giuliani Gets a Medal. Anthropic Slips.
preview_text: The holiday travel rush, a $41 billion drug deal and why Bangladesh garment workers won a raise.
description: TSA expects 17.6 million flyers over Thanksgiving week. Trump gave Rudy Giuliani the Medal of Freedom, and Anthropic slipped below its IPO price.
contents_extra: Why Bangladesh garment workers won a 36% raise, trivia and your poll

stories.title: TSA Expects 17.6 Million Flyers as the Holiday Rush Begins

photo.alt: Traffic on a wet highway at night; file photo.

paragraphs: TSA said it expects to screen about 17.6 million air travelers from Tuesday, Nov. 24, through Monday, Nov. 30. The agency projects more than 3 million passengers on Sunday, Nov. 29, the busiest day of the period. It urges arriving two hours early for domestic flights.

NOAA forecast scattered showers and a few thunderstorms in the Southeast on the busy pre-Thanksgiving travel day. Later Wednesday, wet snow and rain are possible in the mid-Mississippi Valley. Flood watches cover Florida's east coast, including Miami, through Thursday, NBC News reports.

stories.title: Trump Gives Rudy Giuliani the Presidential Medal of Freedom

photo.alt: The White House under a cloudy sky; file photo.

paragraphs: President Trump presented Rudy Giuliani with the Presidential Medal of Freedom on Tuesday, CBS News reports. The White House praised his work as a federal prosecutor and as New York City mayor. Giuliani said he was "honored and humbled."

Giuliani represented Trump in efforts to overturn the 2020 election results, NBC News reports. That work led to his disbarment in New York and Washington, D.C. Cases against him in Georgia and Arizona were dropped. He has denied the allegations.

stories.title: Anthropic Falls Below Its IPO Price as Tech Stocks Slide

photo.alt: A stock chart on a laptop screen; file photo.

paragraphs: Anthropic shares fell below their IPO price after a 13% sell-off Tuesday, CNBC reports. Trading under $76, the stock was 8.5% below its offering level. It took just four days, compared with 21 trading days for SpaceX.

The Nasdaq and the S&P 500 closed lower Tuesday as AI shares gave back gains, Reuters reports via NBC News. As of early Wednesday, S&P 500 futures were down 1.4%, CNBC reports. Traders were also looking ahead to fresh October inflation data, CNBC said.

stories.title: Sanofi Agrees to Buy Insmed for $41 Billion

photo.alt: Assorted pills in blister packs; file photo.

paragraphs: Sanofi said Tuesday it agreed to acquire U.S. drugmaker Insmed for $175 per share in cash. The company put the total at $41.0 billion, or EUR 37.6 billion. The deal adds two commercialized respiratory medicines.

If closed, it would be the biggest pharma deal since Pfizer bought Seagen in December 2023, CNBC reports. Insmed shares closed up 14.1% Tuesday, CNBC reports. Sanofi said it expects the deal to close in the first half of 2027.

deep_dive.title: Why Bangladesh Garment Workers Won a 36% Raise

photo.alt: A worker at an industrial sewing machine; file photo.

paragraphs: What happened. Bangladesh raised the minimum monthly wage for entry-level garment workers by 36% on Wednesday, AP reports. The new floor is 17,000 takas, about $136, up from 12,500 takas. It came after weeks of violent protests that closed factories and disrupted production. Workers had demanded the minimum wage be doubled.

Why it matters. Garments make up about 80% of Bangladesh's exports, mostly to the United States and Europe, AP reports. The sector directly employs about 4 million workers, mostly women from rural areas. Bangladesh is the world's second-largest garment exporter, behind China, Al Jazeera reports, which shapes clothing supply chains.

What each side says. Protesters had asked for 30,000 takas, Al Jazeera reports. A labor representative on the wage board called the outcome "not entirely bad" and urged workers back to factories. A manufacturers group said the protests cost the industry an estimated $428 million in losses. It said $254 million in orders moved to other countries.

What comes next. The wage hike will take effect in December, with new salaries paid in January, Al Jazeera reports. The six-member board approved the wage in a 4-2 vote, AP reports. It was not immediately clear if workers would accept the new structure after weeks of protests, AP reports.

World view: Pakistan's first astronaut reaches orbit. Muhammad Zeeshan Ali became the first foreign astronaut to board China's Tiangong space station; Al Jazeera reports.
Britain sanctions the Houthis. The UK designated the group under its Yemen sanctions regime and targeted four senior figures it accuses of serious abuses; Reuters reports.
Dozens are feared trapped in an Indonesian mine. Rescuers are searching for dozens of workers feared trapped in a flooded unauthorized gold mine in West Java; Al Jazeera reports.
The UK warns of Russian sabotage. Officials said companies supplying equipment to Ukraine's armed forces could be targets; Al Jazeera reports.
Need to know: Two turkeys get pardons. President Trump pardoned Freedom and Feathers on Tuesday in the annual White House tradition; CBS News reports.
Officials debate targeting Iran's leaders. Trump administration officials are internally debating it, according to a U.S. official and a person with knowledge of the talks; NBC News reports.
Six injectable drugs are recalled. Par Health is recalling 46 lots over particulate matter detected in certain lots, the company said; per an FDA-posted notice.
The WHO chief urges an end to the U.S. fuel blockade on Cuba. Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus warned the sanctions were endangering children's lives during a visit to Cuba; Al Jazeera reports.
Money & markets: Trump Accounts pass $1 billion from family and friends. Friends and family contributions topped $1 billion, bringing total deposits above $9 billion, the Treasury said; CNBC reports.
Asian markets tumble. South Korea's Kospi plunged 6.2% and Japan's Nikkei 225 dropped 2.8% on Wednesday as AI doubts swirled; Al Jazeera reports.
OakNorth wins a U.S. bank charter. The U.K. lender got approval to buy Michigan-based Community Unity Bank subject to an $80 million capital injection at closing; CNBC reports.
Buffer funds draw attention. These ETFs aim to blunt losses as the Nasdaq Composite slid nearly 12% in the fourth quarter; CNBC reports.
Future frontiers: Hubble captures a barred spiral galaxy. NGC 4394 sits about 55 million light-years away in the Virgo Cluster; NASA said.
NASA locks in key parts of its nuclear spacecraft. SR-1 Freedom is targeted to launch in 2028 to demonstrate nuclear electric propulsion in deep space; NASA said.
A cargo ship heads to the space station. Progress 97 launched from Kazakhstan with about three tons of food, fuel and supplies; NASA said.
Instagram adds Meta's Muse to DMs. Users can now chat with the AI agent inside a direct message thread; TechCrunch reports.
The score: Indiana drops out of the CFP top 12. The defending champion Hoosiers fell six spots to No. 14 in rankings released Tuesday night; ESPN reports.
Real Madrid routs PSV. Kylian Mbappe scored twice in a 5-1 win, Madrid's fifth straight Champions League victory; ESPN reports.
Manchester City draws again. City drew 2-2 with Napoli and has won just one of its last seven matches in all competitions; ESPN reports.
The Celtics stay unbeaten in NBA Cup play. Boston beat Washington 131-116 after a 46-point second quarter; ESPN reports.
Life & culture: Aquamarine is getting a series. Emma Roberts will reprise her role as Claire in a new TV series inspired by the 2006 film; ABC News reports.
Jordan Firstman opens up about Club Kid. He said his directorial debut came from a major heartbreak; ABC News reports.
Two men are charged in a royal burglary case. Police charged them over an alleged burglary Monday evening at Prince William and Princess Kate's Anmer Hall home; ABC News reports.
Dancing with the Stars plans a 60-show tour. The tour will kick off Jan. 21 in New Hampshire and wrap April 11 in Georgia; ABC News reports.

trivia.question: Which day does TSA project will be the busiest of the Thanksgiving travel period?
trivia.explanation: D. Sunday, Nov. 29. TSA projects more than 3 million passengers that day, the agency said.
